html: † טָֽבְאַ֑ל n.pr.m. (appar. pointed to mean good-for-nothing (אַל as neg.) v. De Di Du StaGesch. i. 590, orig. טָֽבְאֵל; Ol§ 91 d Köii, 537 al. think -אַ֑ל simply pausal form)—Aramean, whose son Peḳaḫ and Reṣin proposed to make king of Jerus. in place of Ahaz; only בֶּן־מָֽבְאַ֑ל Is 7:6 (WklAlttest. Untersuch. 1892, 74 identif. with Reṣin, comparing טַבְרִמֹּן father of Benhadad).
